thread:
Alex: quick heads-up — I'm prototyping a mixed nodepool (p4d + g5) for batch inference. want to validate eviction + capacity-reservation behavior before I open the PR.

Maria: nice. are you planning to use Capacity Reservations (CR) or just reserved instances? we hit weird edge cases with CR targeting last quarter.

Alex: using capacity_reservation = true in TF for the critical pool, and spot fallback for burst. here's the TF-ish snippet I'm testing locally:

```
resource "aws_instance" "gpu" {
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  capacity_reservation_specification {
    capacity_reservation_preference = "open"
    capacity_reservation_target {
      capacity_reservation_id = var.cr_id
    }
  }
  instance_market_options {
    market_type = var.use_spot ? "spot" : "on-demand"
  }
  tags = {
    nodepool = "gpu-batch"
  }
}
```

Sam: couple notes: 1) for EKS nodegroups we prefer taints+labels so workloads land on reserved nodes, 2) autoscaler config needs the custom label to pick the right groups, and 3) ensure termination handler DaemonSet for spot nodes.

Jess: also add IAM permissions for the node role to call DescribeCapacityReservations and DescribeInstances — bootstrap logic reads CR metadata.

Alex: good call. where do we store CR IDs? var.cr_id for now but should be persisted in SSM/Secrets Manager — any org preference?

Maria: we put CR IDs in SSM at `/infra/gpu/capacity_reservations`. cross-account CRs require KMS-encrypted secrets and audit tags (ops requested that).

Sam: don't forget the eviction/termination flow: cordon -> drain -> migrate jobs. we use a preempt handler + a small controller that marks pods for reschedule, and a DaemonSet that listens to the spot termination notice.

Alex: example command I plan to use during testing:
```
kubectl apply -f manifests/spot-termination-handler.yaml
kubectl cordon node/<node-name>
kubectl drain node/<node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

Alex: pinging infra-oncall @Sam @Jess — can one of you quick-review this before I open the PR? plan will touch TF nodegroup resource, IAM role, and SSM wiring.

Jess: I'll take a look in ~1h. quick Q: do we use the built-in `kubernetes.io/instance-type` or a custom label for affinity? prefer a custom label so the autoscaler filter is simpler.

Sam: +1 for custom label: `node.redwood.io/gpu-pool=reserved`. that keeps provider labels untouched and makes discovery deterministic.

Alex: cool, I'll switch to `node.redwood.io/gpu-pool=reserved` for reserved nodes and `node.redwood.io/gpu-pool=spot` for the burst pool. rollout plan: create reserved pool, cordon & drain spot pool with maxUnavailable=10% for safe rollout.

infra-bot: CI plan created for branch alex/cr-provisioning — plan link: https://ci.internal/runs/7890 :white_check_mark:

Maria: test requests — please run a k6 startup latency test against the group-to-group scale-up path and capture time-to-ready for pods (warm KV cache matters).

Alex: will add k6 script and a TF `locals` block that maps instance_type -> cr_id to avoid manual lookup.

Jess: will add the IAM snippet and tag/audit requirement to the PR comments. If infra-oncall approves, tag ops for cross-account KMS review.

Alex: thanks all :rocket: I'll open PR #3421 shortly and @mention you in the description with the plan link and test steps.
